description.narrative: I likhet med tidigare program med det maliska nationella institutet för statistik (INSTAT) är det övergripande målet med denna insats att ytterligare stärka kvalitet, tillgänglighet och analys av statistik för användares behov i Mali. Insatsen kommer att pågå från januari 2020 till december 2023. Den föreslagna insatsen består av två huvudkomponenter: En ekonomisk stödkomponent direkt till INSTAT och en teknisk supportkomponent för INSTAT via SCB. De tre huvudsakliga specifika målen för insatsen är följande: o Stärka planering och förvaltning av det nationella statistiksystemet o Bidra till att ytterligare förbättra produkter och kvaliteten av prioriterad statistik (ekonomisk, social och miljörelaterad statistik), o Öka tillgängligheten av data för beslutsfattande och övervakning av nationella och internationella utvecklingsplaner. För att uppnå detta kommer INSTAT och SCB att ta fram social, ekonomisk och miljörelaterad statistik, stärka ledningens kapacitet (administrativ och teknisk personal) samt publicera och sprida statistiska produkter.

Similarly to previous programs with the Malian National institute for Statistics (INSTAT), the overall objective of this contribution is to further strengthen the quality, availability and analysis of statistics for the needs of users in Mali. This program will run from January 2020 to December 2023. The proposed intervention consists of two main components: A financial support component directly to INSTAT, and a technical support component for INSTAT via the Swedish Statistics Central Bureau Statistics (SCB). The following are the three main specific objectives of the intervention o Strengthen the planning and management of the national statistics system o Contribute to further improve products and quality of priority statistics (economic, social and environmental statistics), o Increase availability of data for decision making and monitoring of national and international development plans. To achieve this, INSTAT and SCB will on the production of social, economic and environmental statistics, strengthening the capacities of the management (administrative and technical staff) and the publication and dissemination of statistical products.

The objectives of the intervention are the following: 1. Strengthen the planning and management of the national statistics system 2. Contribute to further improve products and quality of priority statistics (economic, social and environmental statistics), 3. Increase availability of data for decision making and monitoring of national and international development plans. At the end of the intervention, the following specific results are expected: improvement of the effectiveness of the production process and coordination mechanisms of the national statistics system development of statistics on prices, companies et improvement of the quality of macro economical statistics according to international standards improvement of the reach and quality of social statistics , including key SDG indicators to respond to user's needs improvement of the reach and quality of agricultural and environmental statistics, including SDGs. better availability and friendly dissemination of statistics in accordance with user's needs INSTAT and SCB have revised their joint results framework in order to better reflect the reduction of funds from Sida (in the INSTAT component). The results framework now shows that most of the objectives will still be possible to reach, but there are some achievements that will not be accomplished, such as Update of design and structure of business register. The results framework highlights areas that relate to technical support and financial support, where the former is mostly unchanged whereas the latter is affected to some extent by the reduction of funding.

description.narrative:
Due to the decision taken by the Swedish Government to phase out the Swedish bilateral development cooperation strategy to Mali, the contribution was not extended to a fourth phase. The Agreement with INSTAT ended in December 2023 and hence no negotiation regarding an Agreement Amendment was needed. Nevertheless, as the activity period was not extended the remaining funds, approximately 34 percent of the total budget, were not disbursed. The Service Purchase Agreement with SCB continued in 2024 and the budget regarding SCB's component was reduced with approximately 10 percent due to the phase out of the Swedish strategy to Mali. It is important to remember that SCB's planned results' delivery also depended on the INSTAT component of the contribution, hense SCB suffered not only from the 10 percent cut to their own component but also from the 34 percent cut to INSTAT's.
According to the final narrative report shared with Sida in 2025, drafted by Statistics Sweden (SCB) with input from INSTAT, the following has been achieved during the third phase of the project, 2020-2024.
Outcome 1. Improved efficiency of production process and coordination mechanisms
The project made significant progress in establishing a solid planning and monitoring framework at INSTAT and strengthening coordination across the National Statistical System (NSS). However, budgetary limitations, technical challenges, and legal constraints hindered the implementation of some planned outputs (like time reporting, HR tools, and commissioned statistics). The long-term impact, especially on NSS coordination, will depend on future institutional commitment such as operationalizing the proposed dialogue forum.
Outcome 2. Developed resilience of price and business statistics, and improved quality of macroeconomic indicators pursuant to international standards
Despite some outputs being canceled or unrealized due to lack of funding, pandemic impact, and organizational barriers, Component 2 successfully strengthened Mali's capacity in trade statistics and Consumer price index (CPI). The adoption of statistical tool R (an open-source software for statistics free of charge) and new analytical methods marks a step forward in sustainability and self-reliance. Unmet goals, such as the business register and GDP training, highlight areas for renewed focus in future cooperation.
Outcome 3: Improved scope and quality of social statistics
Component 3 successfully consolidated and strengthened social statistics, especially through long-term support for the EMOP household survey and gender statistics. The creation of a process manual and the second gender booklet are key deliverable that will support future sustainability. While activities in vital statistics were unfortunately not implemented, the project yielded notable institutional learning and increased analytical capability, especially through the introduction of R, see above, and advanced statistical methods.
Outcome 4: Improved range and quality of environmental and agricultural statistics
Component 4 successfully launched Malis environmental accounting, introduced organisation-wide (Geographic Information System) GIS coordination, and laid the groundwork for improved (Sustainable Development Goals) SDG reporting. While contextual limitations restricted some outputs, the component marks a significant step forward in Malis environmental and agricultural statistics capacity.
Outcome 5: More user-friendly statistics available on INSTATs website
Component 5 successfully improved external dissemination of statistics through the launch of a bilingual online database and modern publication practices. While significant strides were made in external communication, internal communication at INSTAT and full IT infrastructure readiness remain ongoing challenges. The updated IT strategy and improved NSS communication framework lay a solid foundation for continued progress.
Longer term results of the collaboration between INSTAT and SCB
Sida documents the following longer-term results from this collaboration that spanned over three periods of support plus twinning work before them (all in all over 15 years of collaboration):
* INSTAT has appreciated SCB's help as a "critical friend" that has contributed over a long period of time and with local presence through longterm resident advisors. INSTAT has appreciated that this was a collaboration between institutions and not a partner that buys consultancy services for them on the international market which is the case with some of their other international collaborations.
* The collaboration between INSTAT and SCB has strengthened INSTAT as an institution that leads the Malian statistics system. The collaboration has strengthened the whole system and has contributed to increased collaboration between different Malian institutions on the topic of statistics. Planning and follow-up within the field of statistics have improved.
* The collaboration between INSTAT and SCB has led to increased presentation of gender disaggregated data.
* The collaboration between INSTAT and SCB has been key to the flagship project of continuously conducted household surveys (EMOP - Enquête modulaire et permantente auprès des ménages) that have increased the knowledge of Malian society and have fed into the national poverty reduction strategy (CSCRP - Cadre Stratégique pour la Croissance et la Réduction de la Pauvreté).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
